title: Cheese Pupusas with Curtido and Tomato Salsa
summary: Soft masa cakes stuffed with melting cheese, griddled until spotted and golden, and served with tangy cabbage pickle and a simple tomato salsa.
equipment: baking tray lined with baking paper

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
boiling water, plus warm water as needed
fine sea salt or table salt
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Pickle
steps.text: Toss 250 g cabbage, the carrot and 40 g onion together, warm 60 ml vinegar, 60 ml water, the oregano and salt until dissolved, pour over and leave for at least 30 min.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Blend 400 g tomatoes, 30 g onion, garlic and chilli until smooth, then simmer with the oil and salt for 8-10 min until slightly thickened, and cool.

steps.title: Mix
steps.text: Combine 230 g masa harina and salt, stir in 480 ml boiling water and 1 tsp oil to a soft dough, and cover for 20 min.

steps.title: Fill
steps.text: Whizz 55 g cotija to a sandy texture, pulse in 225 g Monterey Jack until it looks like wet oatmeal, then shape into 8 balls.

steps.title: Shape
steps.text: Flatten a test piece of dough, adding warm water if it cracks, then divide into 8 balls and keep covered with a damp towel.

steps.title: Wrap
steps.text: Press each dough ball to a 10 cm disc, set a cheese ball in the centre, wrap the dough around it, pinch shut and reshape to a smooth 10 cm disc.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Heat the remaining oil in a non-stick pan over medium-high and cook 4 pupusas at a time for 2-4 min per side until spotty brown.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot with the curtido and salsa.

tips: If the dough cracks badly when flattened, work in a little warm water until it feels soft and slightly tacky.
Keep the dough balls covered with a damp towel while you work so they don't dry out and crack.
Let the curtido sit for at least half an hour so the cabbage softens and takes on the vinegar's tang.
storage: Pupusas are best eaten hot from the pan, while the curtido and salsa can be made ahead and kept covered in the fridge until needed. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
